en.headline: Police to introduce AI facial recognition on SmartView CCTV this month
en.dek: The force said the feature, tested on missing elderly cases and a robbery, will expand coverage toward 60,000 cameras by 2028, with several malls agreeing to link systems.
body: Police will add artificial-intelligence facial recognition to the SmartView closed-circuit television network this month, Senior Superintendent Leung Ming-leung of the Operations Department said. The system is expected to cover about 60,000 cameras across Hong Kong by 2028, though not all will run the recognition function at the same time because of computing limits.

Leung said tests had already helped locate an elderly person with dementia within about 90 minutes of a report and identify a robbery suspect who reappeared on camera. He described the tool as equivalent to additional officers monitoring feeds around the clock, reducing the time spent reviewing footage and freeing staff for other duties. Use requires authorisation by an inspector or above, with subsequent review, and footage is kept no longer than 31 days while recognition data is retained no more than 180 days.

The plan will also extend to private operators this year. Several shopping centres, including those under Sino Group such as Olympian City and Tuen Mun Town Plaza, a Housing Authority mall in Kwai Chung and a Housing Society development in Fanling, have agreed to connect their cameras. Police said the links would speed investigations involving multiple sites by removing the need for separate requests and on-site operators. Leung noted that legal and third-party reviews had confirmed the arrangement meets regulatory requirements, and the force encourages malls to display notices.

As of the end of last month the network had assisted in clearing 2,192 cases and arresting 2,831 people, according to police figures cited in local reports. The first phase focused on government and public facilities; the second phase targets private malls with high foot traffic.

zh.headline: 警方銳眼計劃本月加入人工智能人臉識別
zh.dek: 行動部高級警司梁銘亮表示，系統已測試協助尋回失智長者及偵破行劫案，並有多個商場同意今年內接入，目標2028年約六萬支鏡頭。
body: 警方表示，「銳眼計劃」閉路電視系統將於本月內加入人工智能人臉識別功能。行動部高級警司梁銘亮指出，預計到2028年全港約有六萬支鏡頭可用作識別，但因算力限制不會同時全部啟用。
梁銘亮稱，測試期間曾在接報後約個半小時尋回一名八十多歲患腦退化症的長者，亦曾透過人臉特徵鎖定行劫疑犯再出現的位置並將其拘捕。他形容這等同多了警員全日監察鏡頭，可加快調查並節省人手翻查片段。使用前須經督察級以上人員審批，事後有複檢；影像儲存不超過31日，識別數據不超過180日。
計劃今年內擴展至私人機構。信和集團旗下奧海城、屯門市廣場、房委會葵涌商場及房協粉嶺「嶺．樂活」等已同意將閉路電視接入。警方指，接入後若案件涉及多個地點，可免逐一申請翻看及尋找操作人員，節省時間。梁銘亮表示已諮詢法律專家及第三方機構，符合法規要求，並鼓勵商場加設標示。
警方數據顯示，截至上月底系統已協助偵破2192宗罪案，拘捕2831人。第一階段主要接入政府及公營機構鏡頭，第二階段則拓展至人流較多的私營商場。
